title: Crispy Soy Potatoes with Tuna Yogurt

replaces.change: The bundled 'soy-baked potatoes with tuna sriracha mayo' brushed potatoes with a 50 g soy mixture and bound the filling with 30 g sriracha mayo. This version cuts soy to 1 tbsp (painted on cut sides so little is needed), binds with Greek yogurt instead of mayonnaise (the strict scanner counts mayo as an egg class anyway), and keeps 2 tsp sriracha - the validator's salty-unmapped flag fires for it deliberately. Spinach is dressed rather than blanched.

qty.note: painted on the cut faces only - a little goes further than a brush of marinade
kept for the dish's identity; it has no committed catalog row, so its sodium stays unmapped and flagged

steps.text: Prick each potato all over with a fork and microwave on full power for 10 minutes, turning once, until a paring knife slides in without resistance.
Meanwhile heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Stir the tuna, yogurt, sriracha, ginger, half the green onions and the lemon juice together in a bowl; taste and add more lemon if it sits flat.
Halve the par-cooked potatoes, score the flesh in a crosshatch, and paint the cut faces with 2 teaspoons of the soy sauce - cut sides drink it in, skins do not need any.
Bake the potatoes cut-side-up on a tray for 12 minutes until the edges crisp and the soy glaze darkens; keep an eye after minute 10, glaze can go from lacquered to burnt fast.

While the potatoes bake, warm the vegetable oil in a skillet and wilt the spinach for 1 minute, tossing with the remaining teaspoon of soy. Pile it on a plate; it should still be glossy green, not collapsed to a thread.
Dress the wilted spinach with the sesame oil off the heat and spread it alongside the potatoes.
Spoon the tuna yogurt into the potato hollows, shower with the rest of the green onions, and eat while the skins still crackle.
